summary: Fire Calendar turns 26 years of NASA FIRMS hot spots over Ukraine (November 2000 to yesterday, 2.39 million detections) into one consistent calendar of burning activity. Raw MODIS and VIIRS records cannot be compared: VIIRS on S-NPP reports about 3 times as many hot spots as MODIS Terra and Aqua combined, so the raw record jumps in 2012 with no change in fire activity. Our harmonization model restates the MODIS era (2000–2012) on the VIIRS S-NPP scale at 0.1° × day resolution. Validated leave-one-year-out on 2012–2019, predicting VIIRS from MODIS alone: 7.3% error for Ukraine × month (19.1% for a constant ratio), 3.6% for yearly totals, bias +0.3%. For any area (preset region, any oblast, drawn polygon or point with a radius) and date range, users get a monthly calendar of detections or anomalies (percentile and z-score relative to 2001–2025), daily counts, the current month relative to its norm, and a CSV export. Built for fire and emergency services, foresters and researchers.
details:
What it does
  • Burning activity calendar from November 2000 to yesterday for any area in Ukraine.
  • Area of interest: preset regions (Chornobyl Exclusion Zone, Donbas, Lower Dnipro, every oblast), a polygon drawn on the map, a point with radius, or place search. A custom shape is encoded in the URL, so a view can be shared as a link.
  • Selectable date range; calendar in detections or anomaly mode (norm, z-score, class); daily breakdown of the selected month; month stepper.
  • Comparison of a month with the multi-year baseline (2001–2025) to show unusual activity.
  • Raw sensor record next to the harmonized one, so the 2012 discontinuity and its removal are visible.
  • CSV download of the calendar and of the underlying hot spots.
  • Optional monthly e-mail digest for all of Ukraine.

How it works

  1. ETL (Go): FIRMS archive (MODIS C6.1 Terra/Aqua, VIIRS S-NPP, 2000–2025) plus FIRMS API near-real-time data for 2026, clipped to the Ukrainian border, each point tagged with its MCD12Q1 land cover class: 2.39 million hot spots.
  2. Harmonization (Rust): hot spots are aggregated to 0.1° cell × UTC day × day/night. VIIRS S-NPP is the reference scale: from 25 Jan 2012, the harmonized count is the observed S-NPP count. Before that, and on 51 S-NPP outage days, it is predicted from MODIS as a detected part (VIIRS/MODIS ratio by day/night, month and spatial block, adjusted for event size and fire radiative power) plus a missed part (VIIRS detections where MODIS saw nothing, ~59% of the signal). Coefficients are shrunk hierarchically toward parent strata. Terra-only months (Nov 2000 – Jul 2002) have a separate sub-model. Industrial sources (FIRMS types 2–3) and 112 persistent heat-source microcells are masked. A full run takes ~2 min on 2 CPU cores.
  3. Validation: nested leave-one-year-out on 2012–2019, predicting S-NPP from MODIS only. WAPE 0.073 for Ukraine × month (0.191 for a constant ratio), 0.143 for 2° blocks, 0.203 for 1° blocks; yearly totals within 3.6%; bias +0.3%. Out-of-sample stress test 2020–2026: 10.8% error, bias −0.3%. 90% bootstrap intervals cover 7 of 8 held-out years.
  4. Anomalies: each month is ranked against the same month in 2001–2025; percentile ≥95 is extreme, ≥80 high, ≤10 low; the z-score is also shown. The current month is compared with the first days of the same month in past years.
  5. Backend (Go, PostgreSQL/PostGIS): REST API for area statistics, the map grid and CSV export.
  6. Frontend (React, TypeScript, MapLibre GL): map, calendar and charts.

Limitations

Before 2012, a single cell-day is a statistical estimate; sums over an area and a month are unbiased. Quiet region-months with very few MODIS detections are underestimated.

Benefits and goals

Fire managers get one comparable record instead of two incompatible ones, can see critical periods for their own area and judge whether the current month is unusual. Next steps: extend coverage beyond Ukraine and add NOAA-20/21 as backup references.

Tools

Go, Rust, TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Docker, Caddy, Google Cloud.

Source code

All code is open on GitHub: github.com/glushkov45learners

  • fire-calendar: ETL (Go) and deployment (Docker Compose, Caddy)
  • fire-calendar-algorithm: harmonization model and validation (Rust)
  • fire-calendar-backend: REST API, PostgreSQL/PostGIS (Go)
  • fire-calendar-frontend: map, calendar and charts (React, TypeScript)
